'''Giovanni Alberti''' (born March 21, 1965) is an Italian [[mathematician]] who is active in the fields of [[calculus of variations]], [[real analysis]] and [[geometric measure theory]].

==Scientific activity==
Alberti has studied at [[Scuola Normale Superiore di Pisa|Scuola Normale Superiore]] under the guide of [[Giuseppe Buttazzo]] and [[Ennio De Giorgi]]; he is professor of mathematics at the [[University of Pisa]]. Alberti is mostly known for two remarkable theorems he proved at the beginning of his career, that eventually found applications in various branches of modern [[mathematical analysis]]. The first is a very general [[Lusin's theorem|Lusin]] type theorem for gradients asserting that every [[Measurable function|Borel vector field]] can be realized as the gradient of a continuously differentiable function outside a [[Closed set|closed subset]] of a priori prescribed (small) measure.<ref>{{cite journal|title=A Lusin type theorem for gradients|journal=Journal of Functional Analysis|volume=100|pages=110–118|doi=10.1016/0022-1236(91)90104-D|year=1991|last1=Alberti|first1=Giovanni|doi-access=free}}</ref> The second asserts the rank-one property of the [[Weak derivative|distributional derivatives]] of [[Bounded variation|functions with bounded variation]], thereby verifying a conjecture of De Giorgi.<ref>{{cite journal|title=Rank one property for derivatives of functions with bounded variation|journal=Proceedings of the Royal Society of Edinburgh, Section A|volume=123|issue=2|pages=239–274|doi=10.1017/S030821050002566X|year=1993|last1=Alberti|first1=Giovanni|s2cid=122624808 }}</ref> This theorem has found several applications, as for instance in the [[Luigi Ambrosio|Ambrosio]]'s proof of an open problem posed by [[Di Perna]] and [[Pierre-Louis Lions|Lions]] concerning the well-posedness of the [[continuity equation]] involving BV vector fields.<ref>{{cite journal|title=Transport equation and Cauchy problem for BV vector fields|journal=Inventiones Mathematicae|volume=158|issue=2|pages=227–260|doi=10.1007/s00222-004-0367-2|year=2004|last1=Ambrosio|first1=Luigi|bibcode=2004InMat.158..227A|s2cid=121753750}}</ref> This result is nowadays commonly known as [[Alberti's rank-one theorem]] and its proof rests of a very delicate use of sophisticated tools from [[geometric measure theory]]; in particular, it makes use of the concept of tangent measure to another measure.<ref>{{cite web|title=Alberti's rank-one Theorem|url=http://www.encyclopediaofmath.org/index.php/Function_of_bounded_variation#Alberti.27s_rank-one_theorem|publisher=Encyclopedia of Mathematics|access-date=June 12, 2013}}</ref><ref>{{cite book|publisher=UMI Springer Lecture Notes in Mathematics|doi=10.1007/978-3-540-76781-7_2|title = Transport Equations and Multi-D Hyperbolic Conservation Laws|volume=5|pages=61–74|series = Lecture Notes of the Unione Matematica Italiana|year = 2008|last1 = De Lellis|first1 = Camillo|isbn=978-3-540-76780-0|chapter=A Note on Alberti's Rank-One Theorem}}</ref> Subsequently, Alberti has given contributions to the study of various aspects of Ginzburg-Landau vortices and of the continuity equation.<ref>{{cite web|title=Caccioppoli prize citation|url=http://umi.dm.unibo.it/caccioppoli/vincitori-en.html#2002|publisher=Italian Mathematical Union|access-date=May 5, 2013|archive-date=October 11, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171011071928/http://umi.dm.unibo.it/caccioppoli/vincitori-en.html#2002}}</ref>

==Recognitions==
Alberti has been awarded the [[Caccioppoli Prize|Caccioppoli prize]] in 2002 and has been an invited speaker at the fourth [[European Congress of Mathematics]]. He has also been awarded the [[Ordine del Cherubino]] by the [[University of Pisa]] during the 2024 award ceremony.
